# LittleWhale headless adaptations

Source: local `.tmp/LittleWhale`, commit `f21613fe86762f34d0f31c1a91c7a8aefd9acd19` (canonical DeepSeek Harness snapshot `b150a551b8d465e31e418e1b2eaf5e79bbb7d28e`). The source package manifests declare MIT, while LittleWhale's ownership manifest identifies the runtime packages as adapted upstream and its root assigns GPL-3.0-or-later to product-owned changes. Both the upstream [MIT notice](LICENSE) and the source project's [GPL notice](LITTLEWHALE-LICENSE) and [license reference](GPL-3.0-or-later.txt) are retained. These adaptations do not claim to relicense LittleWhale-owned changes. No UI, product composition, telemetry or coding tools are imported.

| Local component | LittleWhale source | Adaptation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `session.ts` | `packages/core/session/src/{index,surface}.ts`, `packages/core/agent-loop/src/{agent,tool-calls}.ts` | Headless port of append-only history with a compactable surface, assistant/tool continuation and concurrent dispatch with ordered result publication. Replaces Cordis registries, scoped events, inboxes and chat turn management with explicit host capabilities and serializable pending calls. This is an adapted runtime, not an unmodified import of the concrete Cordis driver. |
| `compaction.ts`, `tool-pairing.ts` | `packages/compaction/compaction-basic/src/{region,summarizer}.ts`, `packages/compaction/compaction/src/tool-pairing.ts` | Preserves priced recent-tail selection, balanced assistant/tool cuts, checkpoint framing, durable compaction brackets and original history. Summarizes the full current conversation before clearing native reasoning replay from the retained tail. Context pressure is anchored to provider-reported input usage; conservative byte estimates price only the delta since that sample. The summary directive describes an embodied agent instead of coding work. |
| `json.ts`, `validation.ts` | `packages/core/session/src/json.ts`; pi-ai's TypeBox validation engine | Lossless JSON helper extracted unchanged. Standard JSON Schema bounds use pi-ai's underlying TypeBox engine directly without its argument-coercion wrapper. Emergent needs numeric, array and string bounds beyond LittleWhale's smaller raw-schema subset. |
| `server/inference/providers.ts` | `packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/src/{provider,discovery,replay,config}.ts` | Uses LittleWhale's pinned `@earendil-works/pi-ai@0.82.1` dependency for actual generation and native catalogs. Preserves catalog-provider dispatch, native response replay, endpoint-prefix model discovery and a streamed listing size bound. Replaces settings/credential services with a server-owned provider array; adds Emergent's Vast gateway transport and AWS discovery. |

The simulation owns time, physical concurrency, committed action IDs, perception and action validation. Tool promises carry world events; the runtime has no world reference and never wakes a conversation from an external event. Model failures retain history and retry indefinitely until cancellation. Completed tool results and pending calls are persisted before the next inference. Resuming must bind pending call IDs to the host's existing action receipts.

This is the only context compaction mechanism. Private notes and goals remain agent-authored simulation tools; no old plan, journal or movement compactor is used. Compaction retains original events for audit and replay; its model-visible surface alone is replaced. Token metrics distinguish provider-reported input/output usage from estimates. Failed attempts contribute call and latency counts; provider errors do not report billable input usage, so their token cost is unknown.

The host's optional `resumeTool` hook rebinds persisted operations before checking the currently offered tools. Compaction uses a summarization-only system instruction and labels its checkpoint as historical; it does not inherit instructions to act in the world.

After successful compaction, retained messages keep their text, tool calls and results, but drop provider replay envelopes containing old reasoning and signatures. The checkpoint covers those exchanges too. Original reasoning remains in durable events and inference audits; new reasoning is retained normally until the next compaction. Failed or cancelled compaction leaves the conversation unchanged.
